data.text:
**Claim 0: first coronary stent 1986, Toulouse**
- EuroIntervention, The first stent in man (Puel): the first endo-coronary stent went into a human in March 1986. URL: https://eurointervention.pcronline.com/article/the-first-stent-in-man
- PCR biography of Prof. Jacques Puel: the first to implant a coronary stent in humans in 1986. URL: https://www.pcronline.com/Physicians/Jacques-Puel
- Verdict: supported as written (March 1986, Toulouse; Sigwart in Lausanne followed weeks later).

**Claim 1: drug-eluting stents keep scar tissue from regrowing**
- Wikipedia, Drug-eluting stent: the drug coating reduces tissue growth inside the stent; restenosis is re-narrowing caused by scar tissue. URL: https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_coated_stent
- Verdict: supported as written.

**Claim 2: in through a thin tube from the wrist or groin**
- NHLBI (archived) Angioplasty: a balloon-tipped catheter usually inserted through a tiny hole in the groin or wrist artery while the patient is mildly sedated. URL: https://webarchive.library.unt.edu/eot2008/20090506025413/http:/www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/dci/Diseases/Angioplasty/Angioplasty_howdone.html
- Verdict: supported as written.
